newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns PLO of heavy price of armed clash.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns PLO of heavy price of armed clash.

text.p: Israel's southern army commander said in an interview published on Friday that every Palestinian trooper involved in a gun battle with his forces would be killed.
"There will be 30 Palestinian policemen lying dead. Not wounded. If there is an explosion, that is what I want to happen," Yedioth Ahronoth daily quoted Shlomo Yanai as saying.
Yanai's comments came as U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross visited the region trying to revive peacemaking.
"War is war: anyone wearing Palestinian uniform connected to an incident like that -- dies," Yanai said when asked what lessons Israel had learned from September gun battles with Palestinian forces.
"And if he isn't dead, then I will ask an explanation why he is not dead. There are no in-between games here."
Asked if he would use missiles in such a fight, Yanai, whose command includes the Gaza Strip, said he would not because it would "photograph badly". Rather, he would deploy snipers.
"Massive fire photographs badly -- and that is a dominant consideration. A helicopter in the air photographed by CNN again paints a picture of the underdog with a slingshot against a power's might."
But Yanai said the army's approach was to avoid armed conflict with the Palestinians.
"The defence minister and the chief of staff have no intention to create escalation. The opposite. The entire intention is to calm the field," he said.

In gun battles last September, 15 Israelis and 61 Palestinians were killed. The clashes erupted after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu allowed a second entrance to be punched into a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
